distinct_fetches.target: Withhold releases a Jira project lacks

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Key alert resolution on the full (reason, name) pair so a missing→archived switch resolves the old alert, and add a plan_release_alerts test for that transition.
evidence: "a new alert ... per withheld name without an unresolved alert of that reason"
"resolution ... per unresolved release-version- alert whose name is no longer withheld"
findings.finding: The resolution rule is keyed on the release name, but the dedup rule is keyed on the full reason. A name that switches from missing to archived (or back) is still withheld, so its old alert is never resolved while a new alert is added. That leaves two unresolved alerts naming one release.
findings.location: Approach step 5 vs AC 'exactly one unresolved BRIDGE_ALERT naming it'
scenarios: Version 2.4 is missing on pass 1, then someone creates it already archived (or archives it) before pass 2. Pass 2 adds release-version-archived:2.4 while release-version-missing:2.4 stays unresolved.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve every unresolved release-version- alert whose reason is not in the current set of `release-version-<reason>:<name>` strings built from `withheld`. Add a unit test: an unresolved missing:2.4 alert with 2.4 now withheld as archived gives one resolution plus one archived alert.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve unresolved `release-version-` alerts by full reason (name + missing/archived), not by name alone, and add a missing→archived transition case to the plan_release_alerts and integration tests.
evidence: "a new alert ... per withheld name without an unresolved alert of that reason"
"{"resolved": true, ...} per unresolved `release-version-` alert whose name is no longer withheld"
findings.finding: Alert resolution is keyed on the release NAME, not the REASON. A name whose reason changes while it stays withheld leaves the old alert unresolved next to a new one. Example: 2.4 is missing, then someone creates and archives it.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (plan_release_alerts); AC 'exactly one unresolved BRIDGE_ALERT naming it'
scenarios: Pass N: 2.4 is missing, so an unresolved alert 'release-version-missing:2.4' is written. An operator then creates 2.4 and immediately archives it. Pass N+1: 2.4 is withheld as archived, so a new 'release-version-archived:2.4' alert is written. The missing alert is not resolved because the name is still withheld, leaving two unresolved alerts for one name.
findings.suggested_fix: In plan_release_alerts, compute the set of current withheld reasons (`release-version-<reason>:<name>`). Resolve every unresolved `release-version-` alert whose reason is not in that set. Add a unit case: unresolved missing:2.4 plus withheld archived:2.4 → one new archived alert and one resolution of the missing alert.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Key alert resolution on the exact reason string (`release-version-<missing|archived>:<name>`), not the name, so a reason change resolves the old alert and opens the new one; add a missing→archived transition case to the alert tests
evidence: Plan: "a new alert ... per withheld name without an unresolved alert of that reason"
Plan: "{"resolved": true, ...} per unresolved `release-version-` alert whose name is no longer withheld"
reducer/_processors.process_bridge_alert stores only uuid/reason/timestamp/resolved, so the reason string is the only identity an alert has
findings.finding: Step 5 opens and resolves alerts on different keys. It opens an alert per withheld name that has no unresolved alert 'of that reason', but resolves only alerts 'whose name is no longer withheld'. When the same name changes reason (missing → archived, or archived → deleted, i.e. back to missing), the old alert is never resolved because the name is still withheld, and a second alert is opened for the new reason. The ticket ends up with two unresolved alerts for one release, which breaks the 'exactly one unresolved BRIDGE_ALERT naming it' acceptance criterion.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (release_alerts.plan_release_alerts); AC 'exactly one unresolved BRIDGE_ALERT naming it'
scenarios: Operator creates version 2.4 and then archives it: the missing alert stays open and an archived alert is added
An archived version is later deleted: the archived alert stays open and a missing alert is added
findings.suggested_fix: In plan_release_alerts, build current = {alert_reason(w) for w in withheld}. Open an alert for each reason in current that is not among the open reasons, and resolve every open `release-version-` alert whose exact reason is not in current. Add tests: a ticket with an open `release-version-missing:2.4` alert, now withheld as archived, gets one resolution plus one archived alert; and the reverse direction.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide how withheld-only outbound mutations count in the `RECON: outbound_differ` totals and `RECON: outbound_update` line, and add `outbound_pass.py`'s telemetry and `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_bridge_output.py` (no-op check) to Scope, with a test pinning the count on a withheld-only pass.
evidence: Plan §4: "`OutboundMutation` gains `withheld_releases: list[str]`, included in the emit condition ... `outbound_pass` builds no typed update when a mutation has nothing dispatchable"
src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:162-168 computes `_ob_updates`/`total` from `outbound_raw` BEFORE the `_has_dispatchable_update` skip at line 188
tests/external/live_jira_dc/_bridge_output.py:86-90: `if any(outbound) ... return 'the differ computed work ... a converged repeat pass must compute nothing'`
outbound_mutation_builders.py:311-329 also prints a `RECON: outbound_update key=…` line for withheld-only mutations every pass
Testing: "pass 2 writes nothing; ... pass 4 writes nothing" covers events and Jira writes, not the RECON totals
findings.finding: Step 4 makes a mutation that only withholds releases get emitted every pass (`withheld_releases` is in the emit condition), and it is dropped only later, when typed mutations are built. The pass telemetry reads the differ output before that drop: `outbound_pass` prints `RECON: outbound_differ total=… update=…` from `len(outbound_raw)`. The live-harness no-op check `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_bridge_output.py::wrote_nothing_problem` (used by `test_reconcile_pass.py` and `test_dc_rich_text_live.py`) treats any non-zero outbound total as 'a converged repeat pass must compute nothing'. The plan does not list this consumer or say how withheld-only mutations should be counted.
findings.location: Approach §4 'Keep it local' / Scope list (src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py RECON totals; tests/external/live_jira_dc/_bridge_output.py)
scenarios: A ticket keeps release 2.4, which the Jira project lacks; each later converged pass reports `outbound_differ total=1 update=1` even though nothing is sent, so a live no-op check on such a pass falsely reports 'the differ computed work'.
An operator or probe that reads the RECON per-action counts sees a never-ending update for a ticket that is steady by design.
findings.suggested_fix: In `outbound_pass`, compute the RECON totals after filtering with `_has_dispatchable_update` (or report withheld-only mutations as a separate `withheld=` count). Add a unit assertion that a pass whose only outbound work is a withheld release reports `outbound_differ total=0`.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
verify command `wc -l` inspects output with `wc` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.finding: Acceptance-criteria / definition-of-done quality issues.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the never-create pin with a structural check over src/rebar/reconciler/adapters for version-create endpoints and client methods, alongside the fake-call assertion.
evidence: "the stateful fakes record every call and a test asserts none is a create"
findings.finding: The 'never create versions' guarantee is pinned only by asserting the fakes recorded no create call. The real Cloud adapter issues raw REST via _direct_rest_*, so a code path posting to a version-create endpoint would bypass the fake's method surface. The assertion therefore cannot fail for the realistic regression and is close to tautological.
findings.location: Approach step 6; AC 'No bridge code path creates a Jira version'
scenarios: A future change adds `self._direct_rest_post('/rest/api/3/version', ...)` in acli_rest.py. The fake-transport test stays green because the fake never sees a 'create' method call.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that scans the adapter sources for `/rest/api/*/version` POST usage and for `create_version` calls, and fails if any are found.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either defer alert resolution until the release add has dispatched successfully, or state explicitly that resolution follows availability alone and that dispatch failures remain log-only.
evidence: "outbound_pass calls it after the diff"
"dispatch_one._update_one_dispatch_releases only logs it"
findings.finding: An alert is resolved purely because availability now says the version exists. Nothing confirms the Jira add then succeeded. If the add still fails (for example a permission error or a 400 on another field), the alert is gone and the failure falls back to the old log-only behavior.
findings.location: Approach step 5; AC 'Once the version exists, the next pass writes it and resolves the alert'
scenarios: The version is created but the add returns 400 or 403. The alert is resolved on the same pass, and nobody sees the ongoing failure.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the retirement path for unresolved `release-version-` alerts on tickets that are unbound, closed or skipped by the outbound diff — either resolve them, or explicitly declare them retained — and test it.
evidence: "reads it once per pass for projects (the bound key's prefix) of bound tickets that have releases or an unresolved `release-version-` alert"
"records sink[local_id] = (jira_key, withheld) for every bound ticket diffed with known availability"
findings.finding: The alert retirement path only runs for tickets that are bound, diffed and have known availability. The plan does not say what retires an unresolved alert on a ticket that leaves that set. That covers a ticket that becomes unbound, closed or deleted, or is otherwise skipped by the outbound diff. Such alerts can accumulate unresolved indefinitely.
findings.location: Approach steps 2–3 (availability read scope; release_mutations_for sink)
scenarios: A ticket with an unresolved 'release-version-missing:2.4' alert is unbound from Jira. It is no longer a bound ticket, so it is never diffed and the alert never resolves.
A ticket filtered out of the outbound diff (e.g. a closed or excluded status) keeps its alert forever even after 2.4 is created.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State what happens to an open release-version alert when its ticket leaves the outbound diff (archived/deleted/unbound): either resolve it explicitly or document that it is intentionally left open
evidence: Plan: "`release_mutations_for` records `sink[local_id] = (jira_key, withheld)` for every bound ticket diffed with known availability"
outbound_pass.py passes OutboundDiffConfig(excluded_statuses={"archived", "deleted"}, ...), so those tickets are never diffed
findings.finding: Resolution only happens for tickets that release_mutations_for diffs with known availability. The outbound diff skips tickets in excluded statuses (archived/deleted) and tickets that are no longer bound. Such a ticket keeps its unresolved `release-version-` alert forever, even though step 2 explicitly pulls in projects for tickets with unresolved alerts so they can be resolved.
findings.location: Approach steps 2 and 5 (sink population / resolution coverage)
scenarios: A ticket with an open release-version-missing alert is archived or deleted: the alert stays unresolved forever
A ticket is unbound while its alert is open: no pass ever resolves it

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that tickets with an unresolved release-version- alert always get a sink entry (an empty withheld list when nothing is withheld), and add an integration case where removing 2.4 locally resolves its alert.
evidence: Step 2 reads availability for tickets 'that have releases or an unresolved release-version- alert'
Step 3: 'records sink[local_id] ... for every bound ticket diffed with known availability'
Testing covers resolution only when 'the version appears'
findings.finding: Nothing tests the path where the user removes the withheld release locally. The plan also does not say whether `release_mutations_for` diffs (and records a sink entry for) a ticket that has no local releases but still has an unresolved alert. If such a ticket is skipped, its alert is never resolved.
findings.location: Approach steps 2–3, Testing
scenarios: The user drops 2.4 from the rebar ticket instead of creating the Jira version. The alert stays unresolved forever.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Log a warning naming the project and the error when a version read fails in read_release_availability, and assert the log line in the raising-transport unit test.
evidence: "a read error leaves that project absent = unknown"
Testing only asserts 'a raising transport leaves that project absent'
findings.finding: A version-read error 'leaves that project absent = unknown', but the plan does not say the error is logged or counted. The fallback then quietly restores the old 400-and-log behavior.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (read_release_availability)
scenarios: Lost Browse permission or an endpoint error on one project disables withholding and alerts every pass with no operator-visible signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each per-project read in try/except, call logger.warning("release availability read failed for %s: %s", key, exc), and leave the key absent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default: names match with the same comparison _diff_releases already uses, and existing alerts are matched by their 'release' field (or by the full reason string), never by splitting on ':'.
evidence: "an intended ADD of a missing or archived name becomes a withheld record"
Alert reason format 'release-version-<missing|archived>:<name>' plus a separate 'release' field
findings.finding: The plan never says how a local release name is matched against Jira version names: exact match, case-folded, or whitespace-trimmed. It also does not say how plan_release_alerts recovers the name from an existing alert, given that names may contain ':'.
findings.location: Approach steps 3 and 5
scenarios: Local '2.4 ' or 'v2.4' against Jira 'V2.4' is withheld or added inconsistently with how the existing diff compares names.
A name like 'R:2.4' is mis-split when parsed from the reason.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add one live smoke check (or a recorded real-response fixture for each backend) proving get_project_versions maps real Cloud and DC responses to {name, archived}, or document why it is deferred.
evidence: "(documented unpaginated)"
"Transports: Cloud reads GET /rest/api/3/project/REB/versions; DC calls project_versions(\"REB\")"
All integration tests use stateful fakes
findings.finding: Both new version-read paths, the Cloud GET /project/{key}/versions and the DC project_versions, are now called on every pass. They are verified only against fakes, with `make verify` run with the Jira credentials unset. No check confirms the real response shape, including the `archived` field and any lack of pagination.
findings.location: Testing; AC 'env -u JIRA_URL ... make verify'
scenarios: The DC client returns Version objects (attributes rather than dict keys), or omits archived for some versions. Every version is then classified wrong in production.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a short back-out note stating how to resolve outstanding release-version- alerts if the change is reverted (for example a one-off resolve script, or a note that operators resolve them manually).
evidence: "writes each as a BRIDGE_ALERT via inbound_translate._write_event_file"
No rollback or back-out section
findings.finding: Alert events persist in the tracker, and only the new code resolves them. The plan gives no back-out note: reverting leaves unresolved release-version- alerts that nothing will ever close.
findings.location: Approach step 5 / absence of a rollback note
scenarios: The feature is reverted after alerts are written, so tickets keep showing stale alerts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add 'archived rule' to the docs acceptance criterion so it matches step 7.
evidence: Step 7: "alert names; retry; archived rule"
AC: "documents the alert, retry and version prerequisite"
findings.finding: Step 7 says the docs cover the archived rule, but the docs AC lists only 'the alert, retry and version prerequisite'.
findings.location: AC 'docs/jira-sync-setup.md documents ...' vs Approach step 7
scenarios: The docs ship without the archived rule and the AC is still checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the AC to: `docs/jira-sync-setup.md` documents the alert names, retry, version prerequisite and archived rule.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State which existing mechanism serializes persisting reconcile passes, so the read-then-write of alerts cannot race, or make alert writes dedupe by reason at fold time.
evidence: "a new alert ... per withheld name without an unresolved alert of that reason"
"outbound_pass calls it after the diff, only when ctx.persist"
findings.finding: Alert creation is check-then-act. It reads the ticket's unresolved alerts from the pass snapshot, then appends BRIDGE_ALERT files. The plan never states that reconcile passes are serialized or that a duplicate is tolerated, so its idempotency depends on an unstated assumption.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (write_release_alerts after the diff)
scenarios: Two persisting reconcile passes overlap (e.g. a manual run during a scheduled run). Both see no unresolved alert for 2.4 and both write 'release-version-missing:2.4', giving two unresolved alerts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a failure-disposition statement: version-read failure is transient (retried next pass, logged at a named level) with a stated treatment of permanent 403/404; the unknown fallback either still sends the add or withholds it without an alert (state which, and why it does not contradict 'do not write such a name'); and alert-write failure is a stated disposition.
evidence: "a read error leaves that project absent = unknown"
"None = unknown, unchanged behavior"
"unknown map → add (prior behavior)"
findings.finding: Disposition is unstated for the new failure arms. (1) A failed project-version read silently degrades to 'unknown': the old per-item add is sent, Jira 400s, and the failure is only logged. That fallback lands in the exact log-only state the plan exists to fix. The plan gives no explicit transient/retryable vs permanent disposition, does not say whether a 404 or 403 (project gone or no Browse permission) is treated like a transient error, and does not say what the operator sees. (2) No disposition is stated for a failure in write_release_alerts, nor for whether it aborts the pass or the dispatch.
findings.location: Approach steps 2, 3 and 5; AC 'A failed version read writes and resolves no alert'
scenarios: The DC versions read fails permanently (permission revoked). Every pass sends an add for missing 2.4, gets a 400 that is only logged, and no alert ever appears. This is silently the pre-fix behavior, contrary to the operator's 'do not write such a name'.
An alert file write raises an OSError mid-ticket. The plan does not say whether the pass fails, the dispatch is skipped, or the error is logged and retried next pass.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the outbound create path sends fixVersions. If it does, apply the same availability withholding and alerting to creates; if it does not, say so explicitly.
evidence: "for projects (the bound key's prefix) of bound tickets"
"`release_mutations_for` records ... for every bound ticket"
findings.finding: Withholding applies only to bound tickets via _diff_releases. The plan does not say how a release absent from the project is handled on the Jira create path for a not-yet-bound ticket that carries releases. If the create payload carries fixVersions, Jira rejects the whole create.
findings.location: Approach steps 2–3 ('bound tickets'); Context
scenarios: A new local ticket with release 2.4, which the project lacks, is pushed to Jira. If the create includes fixVersions, the issue creation fails with a 400 and no alert is raised.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the transport mapping against a recorded real Cloud and DC versions payload (or add a live smoke step), or document why the fakes are faithful to the real response shapes.
evidence: "Cloud reads GET /rest/api/3/project/REB/versions; DC calls project_versions("REB"); both map to {"name","archived"}"
"env -u JIRA_URL -u JIRA_USER -u JIRA_API_TOKEN make verify exits 0"
findings.finding: The new external boundary is validated only through fakes and canned responses. The make-verify AC explicitly unsets JIRA_*. The boundary is the Cloud /project/{key}/versions payload and DC project_versions() Version resources mapped to {name, archived}. The plan gives no recorded real payload and no faithfulness rationale. A mapping mismatch would cause every release to be withheld, or none.
findings.location: Testing 'Transports' bullet; AC 'env -u JIRA_URL ... make verify'
scenarios: DC project_versions returns objects whose archived attribute is absent on older servers. The fake returns dicts with 'archived', so tests pass while production raises or withholds every release.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve a release alert only once the name is confirmed in Jira's observed fixVersions (or has left the ticket's local releases), not merely when it stops being withheld, and add an integration case where the add fails after the version appears
evidence: Plan: "`outbound_pass` calls it after the diff"
Plan Context: "`dispatch_one._update_one_dispatch_releases` only logs it, so nobody on the ticket sees why"
outbound_pass.py writes release alerts right after compute_outbound_mutations, before the typed mutations are built and dispatched
findings.finding: The alert is resolved at diff time, as soon as the name is 'no longer withheld', which happens before the Jira add has been sent or confirmed. If the add then fails (permissions, field not on the edit screen, a transient error, or a version that disappears again), dispatch_one only logs the failure. The alert is already resolved and the release is not in Jira, which is the original 'nobody on the ticket sees why' problem.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (resolution rule) and step 2 (write_release_alerts called 'after the diff')
scenarios: The version now exists but the edit fails for another reason: the alert is resolved, Jira lacks the release, and nothing appears on the ticket
findings.suggested_fix: Have release_mutations_for also record the ticket's still-pending add names in the sink. In plan_release_alerts, resolve an open alert only when its name is neither withheld nor pending: either the snapshot shows it in fixVersions, or it is no longer a local release. Alerts then resolve on the pass after a successful add, which matches the existing pass-3/pass-4 test shape if the test expects resolution on pass 4.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add one sentence to Approach explaining why versions are read up front: archived versions are only detectable that way, the withhold decision stays pure in the differ, and no failing write is ever sent
evidence: Approach describes what to build per step but never why a pre-diff version read was chosen over handling the per-item 400 already observed in dispatch_one._update_one_dispatch_releases
ABSENCE: no rationale sentence anywhere in Context or Approach
findings.finding: The plan gives no positive rationale for its core mechanism: reading project versions before the diff and withholding there, rather than reacting to Jira's 400 in dispatch. The reasons exist (archived versions can only be detected from a read; the decision becomes pure and testable; no failing write is ever sent) but are not written down, so an implementer or later reviewer cannot tell that the pre-read is deliberate.
findings.location: Approach steps 1–3
scenarios: A later change 'simplifies' this by moving detection into dispatch error handling and loses archived detection and the no-write guarantee
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach step 2: "Availability is read up front, not inferred from Jira's 400, because only the versions read can tell an archived version from a missing one, it keeps the withhold decision pure inside the outbound differ, and the bridge never sends a write it knows will fail."
